segments.t: Back in the kitchen, Vika orders a tuna sandwich only to find Max standing right in front of her. Max reveals he overheard her phone conversation with her sister and knows for certain that the baby is his.
Сделайте мне кто-нибудь бутерброд с тунцом.
Сейчас сделаем, Виктория Сергеевна.
Ты сказал, что уезжаешь, ты опять меня обманул.
Как и ты меня.
Я точно знаю, что это мой ребёнок.
Я лично слышал, как ты это сестре говорила.
Я остаюсь ради Евгения Максимовича Лаврова.
Классно звучит, правда?
Отвратительно.
Ничего, привыкнешь.
Тебе нужно прекратить ездить за рулём.
Это опасно для ребёнка.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.

'Someone make me a tuna sandwich.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'make' and 'to me' in a few short words.

'We will make it right now, Victoria Sergeyevna.' Max anchors the line on 'now', while 'proper name' completes the thought.
Ты сказал, что уезжаешь, ты опять меня обманул.
'You said you were leaving, you deceived me again.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'to cheat' places the action in the masculine past tense. Max answers right away.
Как и ты меня.
'Just as you deceived me.' Max anchors the line on 'how', while 'me' completes the thought.
Я точно знаю, что это мой ребёнок.
'I know for sure that this is my child.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'child' without extra filler words.
Я лично слышал, как ты это сестре говорила.
'I personally heard how you told this to your sister.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'said' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Я остаюсь ради Евгения Максимовича Лаврова.
'I am staying for the sake of Yevgeny Maximovich Lavrov.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'proper name'.
Классно звучит, правда?
'Sounds great, right?' The meaning hinges on 'great' working together with 'really' in spoken Russian.
Отвратительно.
'Disgusting.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'disgusting' and 'disgusting' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
Ничего, привыкнешь.
'That is alright, you will get used to it.' Max anchors the line on 'nothing', while 'will get used to it' completes the thought.
Тебе нужно прекратить ездить за рулём.
'You need to stop driving behind the wheel.' In Russian, the idea of 'to you' flows naturally into 'steering wheel' without extra filler words.
Это опасно для ребёнка.
'It is dangerous for the baby.' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'child' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

Before Vika can stop him, Max swipes her car keys from her bag and asks Chef Barinov for his old job back. See you in the next scene.
